items.text: Possessing up to 15 g of cannabis or cannabis resin is not an offence (s 6A), and a household may grow up to four plants.

Smoking cannabis in a public place, including bars, restaurants, clubs and most of a tourist establishment, is an offence: a police warning the first time, a XCD 500 ticket the second, and up to XCD 1,500 on a third (s 6B).
Over 15 g remains a criminal offence under the Misuse of Drugs Act.

citizenship.summary: Official naturalisation, descent and dual-citizenship rules in Antigua and Barbuda, for an Australian passport holder.

facts.label: Dual citizenship (destination rule)
facts.text: Whether the destination allows dual citizenship should be confirmed on the official nationality pages. Do not assume that a residence permit leads to citizenship, or that Australia's rule applies there.

facts.label: Citizenship by descent
facts.text: Many countries have a descent route with official documentary conditions. Confirm eligibility on the official nationality pages before planning around it.

facts.label: Official authority
facts.text: Start with Immigration Department, Antigua and Barbuda for official naturalisation, descent and dual-citizenship rules.

citizenship.notes: Australian law also matters: Australia allows its citizens to hold another citizenship. That does not change the destination country's own dual-citizenship rules.
